text: Harlow Creek Logistics' landing zone, network, ADRs, and DR plan used every chapter of this course, not just this capstone chapter. This lesson traces each decision back to the chapter that made it possible, then closes the Advanced Specialization stage and names what comes next.

Chapter 1's Well-Architected vocabulary is why blast radius and tradeoffs needed no introduction in Lesson 29. Chapter 2 is the entire reason that lesson exists in the shape it does -- management groups and subscription boundaries chosen by blast radius, not org chart. Chapter 3's hub-and-spoke topology and Chapter 4's tiered RTO/RPO and real DR testing are the backbone of both lab lessons, and Chapter 5's guardrails-as-policy is why those guardrails were never just a wiki page.

Chapter 6 gave Lesson 30 its ADR format and the discipline of writing an uncomfortable consequence down on purpose. Chapter 7 is the lens Lesson 31 is told through: a review board can ask real, substantive questions and still miss an entire category of risk, because the checklist itself was shaped around application tiers with no line item for shared infrastructure.

This course is the fourth and last course in the Advanced Specialization stage: Terraform and Bicep for declaring infrastructure as code, Docker and Kubernetes for packaging and orchestrating what runs on it, Cloud Operations and FinOps for keeping it observable and cost-accountable, and this capstone for designing, documenting, and defending the whole system those three pieces live inside.

The Advanced Specialization stage is now complete. The path's next stage, Expert Specialization, contains four courses that build on everything here but not on each other, so they can be taken in any order: Advanced Platform Engineering, GitOps and CI/CD; Hybrid and Multi-Cloud Enterprise Architecture; AI Cloud Infrastructure, GPU Computing and MLOps; and Advanced Site Reliability Engineering, Disaster Recovery and Resilience.

Hybrid and Multi-Cloud Enterprise Architecture extends this chapter's landing zone thinking across cloud providers and on-premises environments. Advanced SRE, Disaster Recovery and Resilience takes Lesson 30's RTO and RPO discipline further -- exactly the kind of rigor that would have caught Prairiewind's gap before it became an eleven-hour outage. Enterprise Cloud Architecture and Advanced Capstone is complete; the Expert Specialization stage starts next.
